Resolves #19637

The release now takes the path every other change takes.
- `publish.mjs prepare --ticket <N> --body-file <path>` commits the release to `release/v<version>` and opens a PR to `dev`. That PR resolves the preparation leaf #N, and its body is checked against #N before anything is built.
- The `dev` ruleset's required checks and CodeQL run on that PR, and the operator's merge is the one human step.
- `publish.mjs finish` then squashes the merge commit onto `main` and creates the GitHub release on that commit, with the atomic-commit line in its body. `npm-publish.yml` publishes from the release event.
- The cut's own record (#19652) is not the PR's close target. It stays open until `finish`, npm and the Portal are verified.

Each phase reads the remote state through `releaseState.mjs` and continues from there. A failed read stops the phase, because an unknown never passes for an absence. A present branch, PR or tag is reused only when it is the one this release prepared or merged, and a missing identity refuses instead of skipping that comparison. A GitHub release counts as done only when its tag is the merged release PR's merge commit. A release published outside this workflow, such as 13.2.0, is refused rather than reported as finished. `--rehearse` reports every gate (a failed read shows as ❌ unknown) and changes nothing.

Evidence: L2 (production readers against a scripted command boundary, live `--rehearse` against the real rules and tickets) → L3 required for AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 (a real cut). Residual: AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-7 at the 13.3.0 cut. Residual-Owner: #19652 (the 13.3.0 cut record).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `publish.mjs` has no `git push origin dev`. `prepare` pushes only `release/v<version>` and opens a PR with `--base dev`. The live `--rehearse` reads `dev`'s rules (`code_scanning, non_fast_forward, deletion, required_status_checks; bypass: never`) and reports that `dev` is not pushed to. The full proof needs the 13.3.0 cut (Post-Merge Validation). |
| AC-2 | Ran as `neo-opus-grace` (maintain, `current_user_can_bypass: never`): the account, permission, rules, refs and pre-push gates all pass. `main` carries no rules, so `finish`'s fast-forward squash push needs no bypass. The release PR's merge is the only operator step. The runbook text lives in neomjs/neo-agent-skills#172. |
| AC-3 | `finish` pushes with `git push --no-verify origin <sha>:refs/heads/main`. The comment next to it says why: the squash flattens every reviewed change since the last release, and `check-spec-retirement` fails such a commit by construction. |
| AC-4 | `finish` reads the note at the merge commit (`git show <mergeCommit>:.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v<version>.md`), strips the stamp with `getReleaseNoteParts`, and appends the atomic-commit line to the release body. It makes no second `dev` commit. `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs` pins the merge-commit read. The Portal check follows after the content sync. |
| AC-5 | `ReleaseState.spec.mjs` (19 cases) runs the production readers through a scripted command runner. Reads that fail throw `ObservationError` instead of reading as absent: a PR lookup with HTTP 502, a release lookup with HTTP 403, a failed ref listing, a failed `git status`, a rules read with HTTP 403. A proven absence (an HTTP 404 release, an empty ref listing) reads as fresh. Every step of both phases is covered. A pushed branch or open PR is reused only when it is the local candidate, and refused when there is none. `finish` accepts an existing tag only on the merge commit, which covers a tag-created, release-missing retry. In both phases, an existing release is refused when no merged release PR produced it or its tag is missing. |
| AC-6 | Live: `prepare --rehearse --ticket 19652 --body-file <a body claiming "No structured ACs">` reports `❌ release PR body: #19652 has 4 acceptance criteria, and the AC Evidence table has 0 rows` and exits 1. At today's `package.json` (13.2.0, released by the old flow), both phases also report `❌ release refs  the GitHub release exists, but no merged release PR produced it: it was published outside this workflow (bump package.json)`. `finish --rehearse` exits 1 on that gate alone, and every other gate passes. Neither changes `git status`. The runbook step is in neomjs/neo-agent-skills#172. |
| AC-7 | `npm-publish.yml` already uses npm Trusted Publishing: `id-token: write`, no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, and a comment explaining that a token env would override OIDC. The 13.3.0 publish run confirms it (Post-Merge Validation). |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Close target.** The release PR resolves a preparation leaf (`--ticket`), because `baseline / PR body` is a required context and wants exactly one `Resolves`. The PR body is author-written (`--body-file`), like any PR, and is checked against that leaf's ACs and the PR-body lint. The cut record #19652 stays open for the post-merge evidence. #19637 carries the CLI Contract Ledger, and its real-cut ACs point at #19652.
- **Tag target.** The tag sits on the release PR's merge commit, not on `dev`'s tip, so later merges can't enter the release.
- **Stopped before committing.** A run that stopped before committing tells the operator to delete the stale local branch. The ticket's resume AC covers pushes only.
- **Runbook wording.** It lives in the `neo-agent-skills` package (neomjs/neo-agent-skills#172) and merges after this PR.

## Test Evidence
- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/release/`: 31 passed. That covers the 19 `ReleaseState.spec.mjs` cases, with the command-boundary fault, binding and body-versus-ticket controls, and the merge-commit read in `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs`.
- Live rehearsals: both phases as `neo-opus-grace`; output above.
- Output shapes checked against live data:
  - a missing release returns `HTTP 404` on stderr, and a missing local ref exits 1 with no output;
  - `git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/13.2.0 refs/tags/13.2.0^{}` lists the lightweight tag;
  - `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json mergeCommit,headRefOid` returns the merged #19648 and `[]` for none.
- `check-engine-brain-boundary` (0 crossings), `check-ticket-archaeology` (0) and `check-file-sizes` (0 violations).

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] 13.3.0 cut (#19652): with a preparation leaf and its body, `prepare --rehearse` passes, then `prepare` opens the release PR, and its required checks run with no bypass.
- [ ] After the operator merges: `finish` squashes onto `main`, the GitHub release carries the atomic-commit line, and `npm-publish.yml` publishes through OIDC.
- [ ] Once the content sync archives the release, the Portal's 13.3.0 notes route shows the atomic-commit line.
